title: carlina corymbosa subsp. major
intro: Carlina corymbosa subsp. major, commonly known as the alpine hawk's beard, is a plant species belonging to the sunflower family (Asteraceae). It is native to the mountainous regions of Europe and has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Carlina corymbosa subsp. major include wound healing, pain relief, and gastrointestinal protection, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents such as sesquiterpene lactones, flavonoids, and phenolic acids. These bioactive constituents have been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities, making Carlina corymbosa subsp. major a promising plant for the development of new therapeutic agents.
